_comment: Pages tools/market_watch.py fetches, and the product names it looks for.
Empty by design: nothing is fetched until someone adds a URL here, and
pointing this at a competitor's shop is a commercial-compliance decision,
not a technical one. Public list prices are ordinary competitive
intelligence; automated collection touches a site's terms of use, so get
that cleared before adding third-party sources.
Each source takes: name, url, and optionally country, brand, product and
owner. Set product where the page is a single product, and the watcher
will stop guessing which name a price belongs to.
Our own shop and public price list are the uncontroversial place to start:
watching those catches our own pricing drifting out of step with what the
team is quoting, which is the failure the price layer exists to prevent.
